photo.description: Map of the southern portion of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Mexico, dated to the year 1843, found in an 1846 book about a survey of the Isthmus proposing the creation of a canal in the region. The map and survey are the result of a project launched by José de Garay in 1842, under a grant given by the provisional government of General Antonio López de Santa Anna. photo.caption: 1850 map of Mexico and Central America, featuring the proposed interoceanic route for the Isthmus of Tehuantepec at the top-left
photo.description: This scarce hand colored map is a lithographic engraving of Mexico. Roughly covers the territory of modern day Mexico and Texas. Inset maps depict the Valley of Mexico, today’s Mexico City and Estado de Mexico (Mexico State). Inset maps along the upper border depict the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, the Isthmus of Nicaragua, and Guatemala. The whole is shows both political and geological features and is rendered in the lovely pastels typical of 1850s Mitchell / Cowperthwait maps. Dated and copyrighted 1850.

photo.caption: Bond issued on 1 August 1858 by the Louisiana Tehuantepec Company
photo.description: $500 bond issued on August 1, 1858 by the Louisiana Tehuantepec Company (formed in New Orleans, USA, in the 1850s to establish a communication line between the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans through the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Mexico), signed by its president Emilie La Sére and his secretary. It has 20 coupons exchangeable for $20 each, which is 8% of the face value of the bond, that is, the interest which is to be paid semiannually (on February 1 and August 1) to the bearer.
